The test image shows a corn leaf with prominent yellow-white streaking/striping running the length of the leaf parallel to the veins. This is a classic viral symptom pattern. Top candidates: Maize_Streak_Virus, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Stewart_S_Disease.

Now I'll view one reference image for Maize_Streak_Virus to confirm.

The reference for Maize_Streak_Virus shows fine yellow streaks along veins, while the test image shows broader yellow-white bands running the full leaf length. However, the overall pattern (lengthwise pale streaking parallel to veins, on a single leaf, in what appears to be a tropical setting with red soil visible) is most consistent with Maize_Streak_Virus at a more advanced/severe stage where streaks have coalesced into broader pale bands.

Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus would show a more irregular mosaic/mottled pattern rather than linear stripes. Stewart's Disease produces bleached streaks from bacterial infection, but typically with a more uniform, washed-out appearance.
